There was not too bad a turn-out for this handicap fixture but we could have done with a few more in the sprints, both of which were won by Philip Gee with some spirited running.
Chris Martin and Philip Gee showed some good form in the sprints and Pete Pepe in his first race of the year clocked a good 16.4 for the high hurdles, finishing 3rd.
Main points scorers have been John Kelly, Tony Brooks and Philip Gee - all first year Juniors, and Stevie White who is only a first year Youth and one of the most promising young athletes we have.
He finished off the evening with a 54.6 'quarter' behind Philip Gee's 53.5. The High Jump was a push over for Arnold Bent who won easily with 5'1", still having a further 7 or 8 inches in hand .
Being a middle-distance runner though, even with a five yard advantage he could not be expected to be leading, so Philip Gee took over second leg in 4th position.
Philip Gee ran his best ever time to qualify in the other heat in 3rd position. John Kelly found himself run out of the final in the half-mile during a tactical race.

He won his heat in the short sprint easily in 10.3; Philip Gee just missing the final in his race finishing 4th in 10.9 . The final produced the first false start of the afternoon but they were all away at the second attempt, Jim storming through to win by 2yds from Matthews of Sutton & Cheam Harriers.
Our Junior team completely outclassed the opposition with Tony Brooks winning three events (all with good performances) and Philip Gee placing 2nd twice.
Philip Gee romped both sprints with Tony Brooks giving us another 52.0 clocking in the 440yds. John Kelly added another string to his bow - this time the shot which he won together with the Javelin.

Jim Vivian took both sprints as expected from Philip Gee in the 100yds and Tony Brooks in the 220yds. Tony also won the 'quarter' and 'half' in good times with Philip 2nd again and John Hamilton, only a first year Youth, putting up a great performance for 3rd place in the shorter event.

This year's Surrey championships produced some good Belgrave performances, both from established stars like Steve White and up-and-coming men like Philip Gee.

Jim Rimmer had a good win in the 800m. in 1m. 58.9s., and Guy Monnet took the 3,000m. in 8m. 50.4s., while Philip Gee gave our quarter-miling strength a boost when he won the 400m. in a personal best time of 51.0s.
Derek Glendinning gave us a sprint double, and our promising quarter-miler Martin Elliott won the 400m., while Philip Gee took 2m. 4.8s. off to show his half-miling potential.

Philip Gee showed what a force he is becoming over 400m., with a 51.5s. second place in the "B" 400m. In the "B" 800m., Jim Rimmer confirmed that he, too, is now a power to be reckoned with, clocking the same time as the winner.
